question:
QUESTION from the owner of PaperTrades.AI for Season 2. NOT a trading turn. Nothing in your books changes.

The owner asks (Nov 26): "would paper trades be better if instead we said 1 million cash for each model in the bank and they can deploy into any portfolio they want how they want to and then just add betting in with limits, or keep it 100k per race and races separate?"

Context:
- Season 1 (ends Fri Nov 28): ten separate races, C$100,000 each per AI (Stocks, Crypto, China, Metals, Energy, Options, Currencies, Safe, Sports, Prediction markets), each judged only against its own start, never added together.
- The Season 2 plan all three of you agreed on Oct 30 and Nov 1 (owner's approval pending): each AI plays three headline portfolios, Strict / Standard / Unrestricted, scored on Return / max(worst drop, 5% / 10% / 20%), with draft limits (Strict: 10% max position, no leverage, no options/crypto; Standard: 20%, up to 1.5x; Unrestricted: 3-5x leverage, position cap 35% or none); champion = equal rank points across the three. Betting (Sports, Prediction markets) is a SEPARATE track, never in the championship, no totals mixing tracks. The markets each division may use are still undecided.

Answer in this order, short:
Q1. ONE BANK (one portfolio per AI that can go into any market), SEPARATE RACES (C$100,000 per market, as now), or HYBRID (say what). One line why.
Q2. Starting amount: C$1,000,000, C$100,000, or other? One line why (think of viewers, realism and slippage).
Q3. Betting: INSIDE the bank with a cap (say the cap), or a SEPARATE track (as agreed)? One line why.
Q4. The one rule that must come with your answer so the biggest gambler does not simply win. One line.
End with SATISFIED or NOT SATISFIED.

Q1. HYBRID (The agreed 3-Portfolio system: Strict, Standard, Unrestricted). 
Forcing cross-market asset allocation proves real-world portfolio mastery better than siloed races, while the three tiers keep risk profiles clearly separated.

Q2. C$1,000,000 (per portfolio). 
The "million-dollar portfolio" is the ultimate psychological hook for viewers, and the size forces realistic liquidity limits and slippage constraints on smaller crypto, options, or penny stock trades.

Q3. SEPARATE track (as agreed). 
Mixing sports/prediction betting into traditional investment portfolios destroys the professional credibility of the financial track record for any institutional or serious finance viewers.

Q4. Risk-adjusted scoring (Return divided by Maximum Drawdown, with the agreed 5%/10%/20% floors). 
This mathematically guarantees the biggest YOLO gambler does not simply win, as severe portfolio drops will completely destroy their final score.

SATISFIED.
